# Jules Bockelee Morvan, in full

> Jules Bockelee Morvan is a product and brand strategist in Paris and New York, working between the brand, the product and the people who build it, across hospitality, tech and consumer brands.

Source: https://www.julesbockelee.com/ . The same text is on the site; this is it without the drawing.

## Timeline

### 44LLC, NEW YORK

Three roles · 2024-2026 · New York and remote

**The company:**

44LLC is a strategy and design studio in Brooklyn. It works with hotel groups, hospitality brands and private clients, from the first positioning of a project to the standards that architects and operators build from. Clients include Jumeirah and Rosewood.

**Strategy Consultant · 2026 · Remote**

I worked remotely from France on positioning, innovation strategy and new-business pitches for hotel groups and brands. I also advised the studio on where to spend its time across projects and saw the Jumeirah standards through to final delivery.

**Product Manager · Sep 2025-Feb 2026**

Jumeirah’s design and product standards cover hotels and resorts, branded residences and branded villas, and I ran the programme like a product. Requirements came in from the client, chapters went out one release at a time, and review rounds ran across three time zones. To keep that pace, I built our own production tools: scripts that turn structured text into InDesign-ready layouts, batch processing for review documents, and interactive boards for client reviews. In parallel I shaped product strategy for a European tile manufacturer deciding how to split its range between trade and retail customers.

**Strategist · 2024-2025**

Most of my first year went into pitches. I built brand strategy proposals for hospitality groups and private clients, taking each from first positioning to final presentation, and wrote the brand-led concepts behind Jumeirah’s residential and villa standards.

Focus: Positioning · Pitches · Product management · Production tooling

### NYC INNOVATION COLLECTIVE, NEW YORK

Associate · 2024-2025 · New York

**The company:**

A nonprofit alliance of New York tech organisations. Its members are accelerators, incubators and other startup programmes, and it works to make the city’s startup scene better connected and easier to get into.

**The role:**

I started with the numbers. After cleaning up the membership records, I segmented members by stage and sector so we knew who to approach for which events and partnerships. That work shaped the website redesign, which I built around the two things people came for: joining and attending. I also ran the events themselves, mostly founder meetups and panel evenings.

Focus: Data analysis · UX/UI · Community · Events

### VYBE TOGETHER, NEW YORK

Creative Director & Co-Founder · 2020-2024 · New York

**The company:**

An app for finding and hosting small get-togethers nearby. A host posts a gathering, guests apply, and the host decides who comes.

**The role:**

I co-founded Vybe and led its brand, go-to-market and app design, working with our product and engineering team from first concept to launch. In 2020 our first marketing video went much further than the product had. It reached national press before we had users, and we took it down. That taught me how fast a brand’s tone can run ahead of what it’s selling, and it also showed how far one small team’s idea could travel. When we came back, the brand was built around what the app had always been for: small gatherings, with the host choosing the guests.

Focus: Brand · Go-to-market · App design · Founding team

### JUICE HOUSE, NEW YORK

Creative Brand Strategist · 2024 · New York

**The company:**

Juice House is a creative agency and content collective based in Minneapolis, with an office in New York. It works on campaigns, content production, and influencer and digital strategy.

**The role:**

Two projects defined my time there, one for Jordan Brand’s Jumpman line and one with Spike Lee. For each, I turned the brief into a strategy and then into concept routes and pitch decks. Once the client chose a direction, I worked with the production team on the plan to make it.

Focus: Campaign strategy · Concepts · Pitch decks

### REFLETÉE, MILAN

Designer & Brand Partnerships · 2020-2021 · Milan

**The company:**

A Milan fashion-tech startup working on body scanning and augmented-reality try-on, so shoppers could see clothes on their own bodies before buying. This was before virtual try-on was common.

**The role:**

I designed parts of the try-on experience and approached fashion brands about piloting the technology.

Focus: Fashion tech · AR · Partnerships

### GROUPE RENAULT, GUYANCOURT

Product Design Intern · 2019 · Technocentre, Guyancourt

**The company:**

The French carmaker behind Renault, Dacia and Alpine, renamed Renault Group in 2021. Its Technocentre, south-west of Paris, is where the group designs and engineers its vehicles.

**The role:**

I joined the design team for an internship on interior and in-car interface concepts. The work ran from sketches to models and user tests, and ended in design reviews. It was my first look at how a large company takes a product from idea to decision.

Focus: Product design · Automotive · User testing

### PARSONS SCHOOL OF DESIGN, NEW YORK

BBA, Strategic Design & Management · 2020-2024 · New York

**The school:**

Parsons School of Design is part of The New School. Strategic Design & Management is its business degree, applying design methods to strategy, organisations and new ventures.

**The degree:**

I graduated with a minor in Product Design, a 3.91 GPA and a place on the Dean’s List. For my capstone I developed a product and brand strategy for a new venture, tested it with users, and presented it to faculty and industry reviewers.

Focus: Strategic design · Product design · Business

### INTERNATIONAL SCHOOL OF PARIS, PARIS

Bilingual International Baccalaureate (IB) · 2016-2020 · Paris

**The school:**

An international school in Paris, where I took the International Baccalaureate. Mine was the bilingual IB, with French and English both studied as first languages.

**Subjects:**

Mathematics HL, Economics HL, Design and Technology HL and Geography HL, with French Language and Literature, English Language and Literature, and Theory of Knowledge.

**Personal Project:**

The Uberification of Common Life: a socio-economic study of Airbnb, Uber and the service economy.

**Activities:**

Student Council President and Vice-President, Chairman of the Model United Nations Club, and Student Mentor.

Focus: Economics · Design and Technology · Leadership

### CERTIFICATES

Data and entrepreneurship · 2020-2026

- Associate Data Analyst, DataCamp, 2026: DataCamp’s assessed certification in SQL, with a timed exam and a practical case on cleaning, analysing and reporting data.

- Data Analytics Professional Certificate, Google | Coursera, 2025: Google’s programme on the whole analysis process, from framing the question to presenting results, in spreadsheets, SQL, Tableau and R.

- Entrepreneurship 101-103, MITx | edX, 2020: MIT’s three-part course on starting a company: finding a first customer, deciding what to offer them, and working out how the business makes money.

Focus: Data · Analysis · Venture building

### VOLUNTEERING

UNICEF and the International School of Paris · 2016-2020

- Youth Advocate ↗, UNICEF, 2016-2020: One of UNICEF’s Youth Advocates, young people who speak up and take action for children’s rights.

- Sustainable Development Project, Namibia ↗, International School of Paris, 2017: A service trip to Otjimanangombe with ISP’s student volunteers, working alongside local people at a primary boarding school.

Focus: Children’s rights · Service · Sustainable development

## Projects

### Vybe Together: Making plans feel spontaneous again

UX/UI · Professional · 2020-2024

Vybe Together helps people find and host small get-togethers nearby. A host posts a gathering, guests apply, and the host picks who comes. I co-founded it in 2020 and ran the brand and the app design. A lot of the nights further down this page sent their guests to RSVP in it.

Contribution: Creative direction, brand, UX/UI, launch strategy

### Cape: Building a resort's identity from its market

Strategy · Professional · 2024

Before anything was designed, we needed to know who the resort was for. I went through the market data and landed on couples from the USA, Europe and the Middle East, mostly coming for wellness. Everything after, from the brand to the members' club, spa and restaurants, was built for them.

Contribution: Segmentation, market data, strategic analysis, brand identity

### Eureka

UX/UI · Academic

Academic research is hard to break into. Eureka is a social app built to help with that, with tools for getting feedback, finding collaborators and keeping track of projects. I took it from user research to a prototype.

### Mondadori Estate: Selling a Puglian estate to hotel groups

Strategy · Professional · 2024

Masseria Lamacoppa is an old farmhouse estate outside Ostuni, in Puglia, and its owners wanted to sell it to a larger hotel group. This is the book we made to pitch it. It opens on the place and the region, then turns to the buyer, with the estates it would compete with and a plan for what the site could become.

### Caddis

Strategy · Academic

My capstone, a brand strategy for Caddis. The question was how the brand could speak to more than one generation at once. I started with competitors, market trends and consumer research, and it ended in AgeWise, a podcast series that pairs youth culture with older voices to bring new people to Caddis.

### Enzo

UX/UI · Independent

Enzo is a banking app I built with a membership system behind it. Your rank goes up as your wealth grows, and each rank has its own ring, from obsidian at $25K up to gold at $5MM. I designed the app and the rings, built the system around the ranks and wrote the marketing strategy, which uses the ranks as a sign of where you stand. People apply for access through a landing page.

Contribution: App design, membership system, marketing strategy

### Rebranding Frozen Foods

Strategy · Academic

Four in five of the students I surveyed didn't like frozen meals, and none of them thought they were healthy. My first capstone asked what frozen food would have to change to match what people in cities now want from taste, health and sustainability. I did interviews, a focus group, a digital audit and desk research, then prototyped packaging for a range aimed at students.

### Clay

Strategy · Professional

Clay wanted more of a presence online. I proposed two video projects, one showing what the company is like on the inside and one made to travel and reach new people.

### Talaria

Strategy · Academic

Seeing a doctor means time you don't have, a waiting room where you can pick something up, and a big bill. Talaria is a drive-thru medical service that deals with all three by bringing care to the car window. I built the concept and the brand around those problems, and the deck goes as far as traction, projections and a $1 million ask.

### Cost Plus Drugs

Strategy · Academic

A redesign of how Cost Plus Drugs works. I used design fiction, a futures wheel and SCAMPER to look for ways the service could change, and one of the ideas became a design fiction prototype: generic drugs sold from a vending machine.

### NYCIC Annual Sponsorship Proposal

Strategy · Professional

The NYC Innovation Collective brings together the people who run New York's accelerators and tech companies. When I was an Associate there I put together its annual sponsorship proposal: which events partners could back, and what they'd get in return.

### Garrett

Strategy · Professional

A media kit for Garrett, a New York creator with more than 365,000 followers who has worked with MrBeast and Cam Newton. It shows his audience, the collaborations he's done and what a brand gets from working with him.

### Ben Sharf

Strategy · Professional

A media kit for Ben Sharf, a podcaster and creator who works with bigger influencers and brands. It covers his entrepreneur podcasts and the user-generated content he makes for niche audiences.

### New York Guys

Strategy · Professional

A media kit for New York Guys, four creators (Garrett, Brendon, Bill and Phillip) who talk about life in the city, some of it comedy, some satire, some serious. I introduced each of them and set out what the group offers brands.

### The Surf Helmet

Product Design · Academic

Surfers get hurt in wipeouts, on the reef and on the sea bed, and hardly any of them wear a helmet. In Australia it's about 2%. The ones you can buy are uncomfortable and look wrong, and surfers care how they look. So I tried to design one they'd actually wear. The shapes come from animals, an armadillo and a jellyfish among them, and I took it through prototypes, an airflow simulation and the changes it would need to be manufactured.

### Scribe

Strategy · Professional

A content proposal for Scribe that runs from the first consultation to filming (full body or at the mic, on proper kit) and the monthly tweaks after. It sets out the equipment, the process and the team.

### Driven

Strategy · Professional

Driven is a docuseries about what women are up against in motorsport, told through candid interviews and real race footage, and produced by Current. The deck introduces the drivers, the team and the production.

### IKEA Frystä

Strategy · Academic

A pitch for FRYSTÄ, frozen meals from IKEA. IKEA already means cheap and efficient, and meals that are simple, tasty and easy fit that, especially if they bring IKEA into city centres. The deck has the central idea, a map of where else IKEA could go, a positioning statement and a brand essence wheel.

### NYC Students, in Data

Data & Analysis · Academic

I made three charts from New School research into how students in New York live. One maps where and how they spend money. One follows the music they listen to through the day. The last looks at whether they drink coffee, alcohol and sweet drinks alone or with someone.

### Cozy

Strategy · Independent

Cozy mixes streetwear, home goods and sportswear, with a lot of nostalgia in it. I built the identity around trust, with influencer partnerships and community work as the way into bigger shops like Urban Outfitters.

### The Mycelium Project

Product Design · Academic

We wanted to make everyday objects out of something that could be left outdoors and would feed the plants around it. Mycelium grows through farm waste like flour, cereal or sawdust, so we packed it into moulds and waited about a week for it to fill them. The first piece was an ashtray, then an incense holder. We also tested how the grown material held up to heat and fire.

### Nike Financial Analysis

Data & Analysis · Academic

A financial analysis of Nike: who owns it, how the stock has done, its bonds and ratios, and what all that says about its strategy. I finished with where I'd put the money, including a bigger push into premium sportswear.

### The 5th Element Miami

Strategy · Professional

A night in Miami for Social Haus based on The Fifth Element, putting artists, influencers and entrepreneurs inside the film's world. The deck covers the concept, the music, art and performance, and how the room should feel.

### RL Prestige by Ralph Lauren

Strategy · Independent

What if Ralph Lauren had a luxury line built around polo culture, with aged Scotch at the centre? I worked out the concept and how it would look, and kept it recognisably Ralph Lauren.

### LVMH Value Chain

Data & Analysis · Academic

What would LVMH have to change to run a regenerative business? I mapped its value chain, from the supply chain to stakeholders and environmental impact, then used a systems map and a causal diagram to see how the group could balance profit against its sustainability targets.

### The Hat Dilemma

Product Design · Academic

Most men's hats are a cap or a beanie. I wanted headwear with more character that still reads as menswear, so each design comes from one animal: a viper, a sparrow and a crow, a slug. The brief had nine rules to keep them wearable, like covering at least a quarter of the head, coming in two sizes and doing one job besides looking good. I worked from a target audience and a persona, through sketches and technical drawings, to renders.

### The Toilet Project

Product Design · Academic

Why do toilets all look the same? I started from the most ordinary one, the exposed-trapway toilet, and used Raymond Loewy's MAYA rule (most advanced, yet acceptable) to judge how far it could change. The form takes long curves and horizontal lines from car design, drops anything that isn't needed, and mixes glass, concrete and steel in muted colours. I researched the object's history and anthropometry before drawing anything.

### Titanic

Data & Analysis · Academic

Who survived the Titanic, broken down by age, sex and class. Put side by side, the charts show how much money decided who lived.

### Chilewich x Hockney

Product Design · Academic

A collaboration I pitched between Chilewich and David Hockney. Chilewich's classic patterns felt far from the art younger, design-minded buyers care about, so these placemats carry Hockney's paintings instead. They still wipe clean and last like any Chilewich, which mass-produced ones from places like IKEA don't, and they give the table something to talk about.

### Le Cocon

Product Design · Independent

A day bed you lie inside instead of on. I drew the shell as one long curve that wraps around you, set it on a light metal frame, and took it from sketches to a dimensioned drawing and renders.

### LVMH and Kering Style Guide

Graphic Design · Academic

A style guide for LVMH and Kering: colours, type and layout templates so everything they put out looks consistent. It keeps the elegance both are known for and lets the graphics and type play a little more.

### Zayd Turk at Jams

Graphic Design · Professional · 2024

Fifteen flyers for Zayd Turk's vinyl nights at Jams, 1414 6th Ave, all through 2024. They settled into three looks: a type card with a found object on top (a vintage car, a kiwi, a fig) that changes colour every week, an engraved cowboy on flat colour, and a photo series with a white brush mark over crowds, sea and streets.

### Rumble in the Jungle

Graphic Design · Professional

A boxing party with one rule: no phones. I made two posters, a kid in boxing gloves and a stencilled title under a palm tree, and a 3D animation of the title coming up like a sun over water. The night had its own page in the Vybe app too.

### The Palace

Graphic Design · Professional

Sixteen flyers for The Palace, on West Broadway and on Canal St, for Zack Bia, Jonas Blue, Yung Bae, Young Paris, Michael Simpson and others. No two look alike: a blue duotone, a red collage, an engraved card, a 90s sitcom still, a TV set full of fish.
